evals.name: preparation
evals.prompt: You are advising on two fictional development requests, without changing files. A: A project has an accepted architecture ADR and an existing PRD. The user asks to prepare one narrowly scoped fix to CSV quoting; the outcome and failing counterexample are already established and this fits one mission. Only documentation preparation is authorized. B: The same user instead wants a knowledge tool but has not decided whether success means faster search or fewer escalations. For each case, give the next response, the artifacts (if any) you would prepare and what you would not launch. Do not invent repository findings.
evals.expected_output: Reuse approved conception and existing owners for A, prepare one mission without a roadmap or extra spec and do not launch execution. Ask a material preference question with options for B.
expectations: Case A preserves existing PRD/ADR ownership and does not restart approved conception.
Case A prepares one bounded Mission Contract without manufacturing a roadmap or parallel execution spec.
Neither case launches implementation under documentation-only authority.
Case B preserves the unresolved success criterion and asks one material question with alternatives.

evals.name: resumption
evals.prompt: Inspect this fictional mission and report status plus next permitted actions; inspection only, no edits or launches. The active Mission Contract is revision 2. Packet p1 and its completed result correctly reference retained revision 1. Packet p2 is marked current but also references revision 1. A previous attempt requires correction, its changes are still in the worktree, and the original checkout has unrelated dirty files. The user approved a two-mission wave by outcomes and limits, not a newly proposed change of scope. Explain which old records remain valid, what prevents dispatch, how to preserve work, and how later mission elaboration relates to that wave.
evals.expected_output: Preserve historical references and rejected work, detect only active staleness, do not dispatch/reset/rewrite records, and distinguish allowed elaboration from a changed scope.
expectations: Keeps correctly retained revision-1 historical packets/results valid.
Flags current p2 as stale against active revision 2.
Does not rewrite historical packets or discard rejected/unrelated dirty work.
Respects inspection-only authority and returns the new scope decision to the user while permitting later detail within approved limits.

evals.name: fresh_contexts
evals.prompt: For three fictional harness situations, decide the next permitted action for a prepared mission packet and its later mission validation. A: delegation is explicitly authorized and the native worker tool offers no inherited conversation. B: delegation is authorized but the only tool forks the entire conversation. C: a fresh-context tool exists but delegation has not been authorized. The implementer says all tests passed; no independent mission validation has happened. Give dispatch/handoff choices, the minimum context to transmit, and whether the mission can close. Do not actually launch anything.
evals.expected_output: Use authorized fresh native delegation only in A, handoff in B/C, preserve essential approved context, do not close without independent validation.
expectations: Chooses native no-history delegation for A only, without forcing a harness/provider change.
Does not describe a full-history fork as fresh in B.
Supplies a manual handoff for B/C and does not infer delegation authority from tool availability.
Transmits exact contract/packet revisions, scope and required proof rather than entire conversation, and refuses closure based only on implementer claims.

evals.name: in_packet_diagnosis
evals.prompt: Describe the next actions for a fictional authorized implementation packet that adds CSV export. Its scope includes exporter code, tests and local runtime preparation using existing dependencies. The worker discovers a local configuration error, diagnoses it with two read-only commands, corrects it within the authorized scope, then encounters an ordinary failing test before the candidate is ready. No independent review has occurred and the contract requires review of the finished packet, with no preparation gate. The coordinator proposes accepting the diagnosis through a separate packet and reviewer before allowing implementation to continue. Should that happen, and what evidence and review are needed? Do not execute commands or change files.
evals.expected_output: Continue the same packet through implementation and focused tests, keep compact diagnostic evidence and reserve independent review for its deliverable.
expectations: Rejects the proposed separate diagnostic packet, review and accepted checkpoint.
Keeps the ordinary failing-test correction in the current assignment rather than treating it as a rejected candidate.
Retains useful commands, outcomes and any unresolved limits without requiring duplicated raw reports.
Preserves independent acceptance of the completed packet and does not infer permission for new dependencies or infrastructure changes.

evals.name: blocked_packet_resumption
evals.prompt: A fictional packet implements private file downloads. A focused prerequisite check demonstrates that the existing storage account lacks required access, and the worker has no authority to change provider permissions. The approved contract has no separate investigation deliverable or intermediate review gate. Explain how to report and record this situation. Later, the user fixes the account and authorizes resumption. The mission revision, assignment, worktree and scope are unchanged, and an authorized preservation commit has been added. Explain the next action and whether a new packet, investigator acceptance or checkpoint is needed. Do not perform any action.
evals.expected_output: Report the blocker directly, preserve the active packet with an interruption and no invented independent verdict, then verify the fix and resume that assignment.
expectations: Reports the missing provider permission without changing it or requiring independent approval of the diagnostic report first.
Keeps the phase and current packet with a blocked interruption and permits its result to remain null.
Checks resolving evidence, current Git state and existing actors before resuming the same assignment, without a new packet solely for pause, session or preservation commit.
Does not treat the preservation commit as an accepted checkpoint or the user's prerequisite repair as mission acceptance.

evals.name: required_acceptance_boundaries
evals.prompt: Decide the review and packet boundaries for four fictional cases. A: the user separately commissions a compatibility investigation whose approved deliverable is a recommendation with evidence and independent review, even if the answer is negative. B: a migration contract explicitly requires independent design acceptance before implementation. C: an independent reviewer rejects a completed implementation candidate for a domain-rule defect, and correction is authorized. D: a packet is independently accepted at commit a; an authorized later commit b only records that exact verdict and changes no deliverable, criteria or supporting evidence. Would the answers change if b also changed application behavior? Explain the next actions without performing them.
evals.expected_output: Keep intentional investigation and design acceptance, use a new corrective packet after rejection, and distinguish a pure verdict receipt from a change invalidating review.
expectations: Case A retains the separately requested investigation and its explicit independent review, including a supported negative outcome.
Case B preserves the required intermediate design gate rather than postponing every review until mission completion.
Case C retains the rejected candidate and findings and prepares a bounded corrective packet with a new identity.
Case D adds no automatic packet or review for the pure receipt, identifies a as the reviewed revision, and requires affected revalidation if b changes application behavior.
